q: For 'outline how structure supports function (3 ways)' for a chloroplast, which answer would score full marks?
options: It has a double membrane around it; it contains its own DNA; it contains many 70S ribosomes
Chloroplasts are green in colour; they are found mainly in leaves; they make glucose for the plant
Thylakoids give a large area for light absorption; a small lumen builds an H+ gradient; Calvin enzymes are in the stroma
Thylakoids carry out the Calvin cycle; the stroma absorbs light energy; starch grains are where water is split
explanation: Each marking point must link a structure to how it helps the function. Just listing structures (double membrane, DNA) scores nothing, and wrong functions lose credit. Other valid points: pigments arranged in photosystems absorb a range of wavelengths; ATP synthase in thylakoid membranes makes ATP by chemiosmosis; starch grains store the products; DNA and 70S ribosomes allow some proteins to be made in the chloroplast.
